text:
alex: Customer reported intermittent 429s during a large prefetch job that fanouts to multiple models. Happens in ~10–20s bursts for ~30–90s windows. They say it started after a deploy.
maya: Can you paste the exact curl + response headers and customer org/id? Hosted or Dedicated?
alex: Hosted. Org: jordan-inc. Example request we asked them to run:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"model":"rw-large-1","input":"<prefill>...","max_tokens":8192}'
```
alex: Response snippet they got back (redacted):
```json
{"error":"Rate limited","code":429}
# headers observed: X-RW-RateLimit-Limit: 1800, X-RW-RateLimit-Remaining:0, X-RW-Request-Id: rwd-abc123
```
maya: 1800 looks like RPM granularity. Did they fanout many parallel requests? how many concurrent processes?
alex: They spawn ~40 parallel requests across 2 models as part of prefetch. Each request includes a long context (~15k–20k tokens) as a prefill. They also use streaming. Billing/usage shows a big token spike and then auth/429s for ~2m windows.
sanjay: Important nuance: long-context requests drive TPM (tokens per minute) consumption much faster than RPM. Our limit checks are layered: per-key RPM, per-key TPM, per-model concurrency and per-model queue depth. A fanout of large-token requests can exhaust TPM almost instantly and then RPM shows up as zero remaining. If model concurrency (rw-large-1) is 8 per key, launching 40 concurrent requests will overflow the queue and trigger 429s.
maya: please share request ids / traces so infra can confirm which limiter tripped (rpm | tpm | concurrency). Also confirm whether 429s carry Retry-After header.
alex: Trace ids from the customer: rwd-abc123, rwd-def456. Example response headers included Retry-After: 30 in a few samples. They also reported a couple of 401s right after the peak.
sanjay: 401s likely from rotated keys or short-lived credentials failing under burst, not the rate limiter itself. Billing spike is expected given the token count; not a billing system outage. Check usage dashboard and invoice preview for that org/time window.
maya: Quick repro steps we used locally to validate: 1) run the same curl in a loop with 40 parallel processes on the same API key; 2) observe 429s after ~20–40s; 3) change model to rw-medium-1 and/or reduce max_tokens to 1024 — TPM/RPM impact drops and 429s disappear.
alex: To support team: sample command we ran to repro locally:
```bash
seq 1 40 | xargs -n1 -P40 -I{} curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' -d '{"model":"rw-large-1","input":"x","max_tokens":8192}'
```
maya: Mitigations to recommend to customer: 1) add exponential backoff + jitter on 429s; 2) limit fanout concurrency to <= per-model concurrency (start with 8); 3) use smaller model variant for prefetch or chunk the context; 4) enable prefix caching / reuse KV cache if possible; 5) consider Dedicated if sustained throughput is required.
sanjay: Also note: per-model RPM and per-key TPM interplay is subtle — a lot of short requests hit RPM, few massive requests hit TPM. For long-context batch prefetching, TPM is the more likely limiter. We can provide exact model RPM/TPM and concurrency numbers if customer requests them (requires org id).
alex: I shared the traces with eng-infra (links pasted in PM). Jordan (customer rep) says they'll throttle the prefetch job and test with smaller model variant, will report back.
deploy-bot: rate-limiter patch v1.4.2 deployed to prod at 2026-03-16T21:12:05Z :rocket:
maya: Assigning eng-infra to follow up if they still see 429s after mitigations. Alex, please DM Jordan the quick mitigation list and ask them to capture a sample trace if 429s persist. :thumbsup:
